items.section: 5.3 Fourteen rungs at fourteen primes, and the fold at twenty-four
items.text: A lac repressor protein in a living bacterium is finding its site on the DNA by sliding along it about 45 base pairs, give or take 10, at a time and going through the cell between slidings, and more than 90 times in 100 it is sliding over its site several times before holding there: a macromolecule's going along and across with no prior of its own comparing, at eleven.

items.section: 5.3 Fourteen rungs at fourteen primes, and the fold at twenty-four
items.text: Bacteria meeting lactose in a gut, where maltose always comes next, are opening their maltose genes partly with lactose alone, and maltose first is opening no lactose genes; growing several months with lactose and no maltose following, they are ceasing to open maltose genes for lactose, over their generations of evolving: a sequence of their learning and unlearning at the gene's re-forming, at seventeen.

items.section: 5.3 Fourteen rungs at fourteen primes, and the fold at twenty-four
items.text: A bacterium is comparing its last second with the three before and lengthening its runs going up an attractant: the smallest navigating observing that is closing as a self's own going on is at twenty-three, the cell, its sequence-learning at seventeen, the gene, and below seventeen a going along and across holding its competency as a stable form, with no learning of its own observing yet; whether a prion copying its fold at thirteen is a re-forming below seventeen is still-possibling.

items.sentence: Reach comes of a co-chaining being longer, and width comes of both being co-linear.
items.text: Eastern North American monarch butterflies are flying in autumn to forests in central Mexico, by a sun compass that corrects for the sun's moving, its timing likely mainly in their antennae; how they are reaching those forests is a hard problem of science.

items.sentence: Along and across lie on one line, and that line is each move's own, in neither move alone.
items.text: Green sea turtles in a pool given the magnetic field of a place about 209 miles north of their capture site are swimming south, and given a field from the south are swimming north, toward their capture site; how any animal is sensing the magnetic field, and how a turtle is making a map from it, is a hard problem of science.

items.sentence: A method observes what a sensing returns, valuable and wasteful together, sorting neither.
items.text: Migrating birds are sensing the direction of the Earth's magnetic field, radical pairs forming in cryptochrome proteins of the retina when light excites them the leading hypothesis, its primary sensing mechanism still unclear, a hard problem of science.

items.sentence: A geodesic is a co-chaining a thing floats where a force acts on nothing, curving as relating curves, straight by relating's own terms.
items.text: Data from 21 female European eels going out from the Azores are showing them swimming southwest about 6.8 km a day on average, going deeper than 1,000 metres, six of the 21 reaching the Sargasso Sea; their spawning there is still-possibling to watch, and how they are finding it, by field, smell, current or warmth, is a hard problem of science.

Each navigating hard problem of science, a monarch's forest, a turtle's map, a bird's magnetic sensing, an eel's sea, is a five-dimensional two-directional navigating still-possibling to resolve by bi-moral co-agency: each self orienting from its own side by the sequence of its changing, with its generations and its others, in neither self alone.

Navigating hard problems with their observings: monarch butterflies reaching forests in central Mexico; sea turtles orienting by a place's magnetic field; birds sensing the magnetic field's direction, a light-driven radical-pair mechanism only the leading hypothesis; six of 21 European eels reaching the Sargasso Sea; each still-possibling at Natural Exploring as orienting by the sequence of changing from a self's own side.
